# MacCleaner

> A trust-first storage assistant for macOS. It scans your Mac read-only, shows exactly
> what is safe to recover, and lets you choose Trash (recoverable) or permanent deletion.
> Nothing is ever deleted automatically. Local-first, no ads, no tracking. Signed and
> notarized by Apple. Free tier covers up to 500 MB of cleanup per day (scanning and the
> built-in AI helper, Scout, are unlimited); Pro removes the cap ($4.99/mo, $19.99/yr,
> $29.99 lifetime).

## Key facts
- Platform: macOS (universal — Apple Silicon and Intel). Download: https://github.com/1erkinyagci/maccleaner/releases/download/v0.1.13/MacCleaner-0.1.13-universal.dmg
- Flow: Scan (read-only) -> Preview every item -> Clean (Move to Trash or Delete permanently)
- Classifies findings as "safe to remove" (rebuildable: caches, build artifacts, package
  caches) or "needs review" (personal). Personal files are never pre-selected.
- Sign-in is passwordless: a 6-digit emailed code, so there is no password to reset.
- Subscriptions are self-service via the Stripe billing portal (link in the site footer).

## Q&A
- **How do I free up space on a Mac?** Clear rebuildable files first — app caches, logs, the Trash, and on developer Macs build artifacts like Xcode DerivedData, node_modules and Docker images. Then review large personal files and offload media to iCloud or an external SSD. Rebuildable files regenerate, so clearing them costs nothing but time.
- **What is System Data on a Mac?** System Data (formerly "Other") is macOS's catch-all for files it can't sort into Apps, Photos or Documents: caches, logs, APFS snapshots, disk images, fonts, plugins and developer build artifacts. The safely reclaimable parts are app caches, logs and developer artifacts.
- **Why is my Mac full when my files are small?** Because caches, snapshots, purgeable space and developer build artifacts don't appear in Finder. On many Macs they account for tens of gigabytes.
- **Does moving files to the Trash free up space?** No. Files stay on disk until you empty the Trash. Only emptying reclaims the space.
- **Is it safe to delete cache files on a Mac?** Yes. Files in ~/Library/Caches are temporary by design and apps rebuild them automatically. Quit the app first and delete the contents of its cache folder, not the folder itself.
- **Is it safe to delete Xcode DerivedData?** Yes. It's build output and indexes that Xcode regenerates. Your next build is simply slower.
- **Is it safe to delete node_modules?** Yes, if your lockfile is committed — npm ci or an equivalent install rebuilds it identically.
- **How much space does Apple Intelligence use on a Mac?** Typically around 7GB for the on-device models in 2026, more with extra languages. Turning Apple Intelligence off in System Settings removes them.
- **How much free space should a Mac have?** Keep at least 10–15% of the drive free so macOS has room for swap, caches and updates.
- **How much free space does a macOS update need?** Often 20GB or more for the download plus installation. Clearing caches, the Trash and developer artifacts usually frees enough.
- **What is purgeable space on a Mac?** Data — mostly APFS snapshots and caches — that macOS deletes automatically when it needs room. You generally shouldn't force it.
- **Can MacCleaner delete files permanently?** Yes, but only when you choose to. By default cleanups go to a recoverable holding area, and you can restore any item until you empty it.
- **Does MacCleaner delete anything automatically?** No. Every cleanup is scan, review, confirm. Personal files are never pre-selected.
- **Is MacCleaner free?** There's a free tier with unlimited read-only scans and up to 500MB of cleanup per day. Pro removes the daily cap at $4.99/month, $19.99/year or $29.99 once.
- **Does MacCleaner work offline?** Yes. Scanning is local-first and runs entirely on your Mac. There are no ads and no tracking.
- **Why does a Mac cleaner need Full Disk Access?** macOS blocks apps from reading protected locations such as ~/.Trash without it, so those areas can't be measured or emptied. A trustworthy app explains this and still works honestly if you decline.
- **Is MacCleaner safe?** It scans read-only, shows every file before anything is touched, classifies findings as safe-to-remove or needs-review, never pre-selects personal files, and is signed and notarized by Apple.
- **Does MacCleaner remove malware?** No. It's a storage tool only — it finds and cleans disk space you can safely recover.
- **What's the difference between MacCleaner and CleanMyMac?** CleanMyMac is an all-in-one paid maintenance suite including malware scanning and an uninstaller. MacCleaner is a focused storage cleaner with read-only scans, review-before-delete and a free tier.
- **How do I cancel a MacCleaner subscription?** Use the Manage subscription link in the site footer or on the post-checkout page — it opens Stripe's billing portal, where you can update your card or cancel.
- **How do I sign in to MacCleaner?** Enter your email in the app and it sends a 6-digit code. Enter the code to sign in — there's no password to remember or reset.
